text:
Recent work supports separating persistent interests from current intent. MSMT-LSI (2024) combines temporal embeddings with separate long- and short-term attention networks. A closer routing match, [Hierarchical Long and Short-Term User Preference Modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y), uses dynamic routing to form multiple long-term preference vectors, matches them against recent behavior, and fuses them through time encoding. [D2MFRec (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) combines soft-clustered interests, recent-item weighting, and learned fusion gates; its full method also adds denoising contrastive objectives.

Two 2026 directions sharpen the temporal argument. [MIMAR-SRec, AAAI 2026](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38489), models intent across contextual windows with prototype alignment and adversarial robustness. [DSRec, September 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548), separates full-history preferences from local intent using two state-space branches; elapsed interaction times modulate short-term state evolution, with residual fusion between branches. Multiple sequence windows capture behavioral scale, whereas explicit timestamp gaps capture elapsed time; these are distinct signals.

For the constrained SASRec comparison, a compact hypothesis suggested by these papers is a shared encoder with a few pooled interest vectors, a recent-window query, and a timestamp-conditioned fusion gate. Treat this as an adaptation to test, not an established benchmark improvement. Ablate interest count, routing, recent-window length, and elapsed-time conditioning separately; measure macro validation HR@10 across all four categories under identical splits, candidates, seeds, and GPU budget. The sources support architectural mechanisms but do not establish gains or compute efficiency under the pinned RecHarness protocol.
